title: Toll-Free Number Cost: $1 to $2.15 a Month, Plus Minutes
desc: A US toll-free number costs $1.00 to $2.15 a month at Plivo, Telnyx and Twilio, but inbound minutes run $0.015 to $0.022. A worked bill, 800 numbers, texting.

body:
Short answer. A US toll-free number costs $1.00 to $2.15 a month at the three carriers we checked on November 22, 2026: $1.00 at Plivo, from $1.00 at Telnyx and $2.15 at Twilio. The bigger cost is inbound minutes: from $0.015 to $0.022 a minute to receive a toll-free call, against from $0.0032 to $0.0085 to receive a call on a local number. One toll-free line taking 2,000 minutes a month comes to between about $31 (a starting rate) and $46 at these rates, before taxes and carrier fees.

This guide compares the published prices, works out a monthly bill, explains why an 800 number can cost $500, and covers what you need before a toll-free number can send texts. Prices are the carriers' published list rates as we read them; Twilio's page says "Pricing current as of October 2026."

Toll-free number prices at three carriers

CarrierToll-free number, per monthInbound toll-free calls, per minuteInbound local calls, per minute
Twilio$2.15$0.0220$0.0085
Telnyx (numbers, voice)From $1.00From $0.015From $0.0032
Plivo (numbers, voice)$1.00$0.0180$0.0055

A few details from the same pages change the total:

  • Telnyx charges "an additional charge of $0.10 per month" to add SMS and MMS to a number, and says "Toll-free has different rates based on the calling number," so its per-minute figure is a starting rate. Above 50 numbers a month its volume tiers drop the number price to $0.79, then $0.50, $0.39 and $0.25.
  • Twilio lists $0.75 a month per number for emergency calling as an add-on.
  • Plivo lists its local numbers at $0.50 a month, half its toll-free price.

Why toll-free minutes cost more

The number's owner pays to receive calls on either kind of number, but the inbound rate for toll-free is higher in every price list we read: Twilio charges $0.0220 a minute to receive a toll-free call and $0.0085 to receive a call on a local number, about 2.6 times as much. Plivo's gap is $0.0180 against $0.0055.

On our reading, a toll-free number makes sense when callers come from many area codes and you want one number on ads and invoices; a local number is cheaper per minute when most callers are in one area. If you mainly call out, the inbound premium matters less, and caller reputation matters more; our local presence dialing guide covers the rules for showing local numbers.

A worked monthly bill

A hypothetical business with one toll-free number, paying list rates and taking all of its calls inbound:

Carrier500 inbound minutes2,000 inbound minutes
Twilio ($2.15 + $0.022 a minute)$13.15$46.15
Plivo ($1.00 + $0.018 a minute)$10.00$37.00
Telnyx (from $1.00 + from $0.015 a minute)From $8.50From $31.00

Our arithmetic: monthly number price plus minutes times the inbound rate. Taxes, regulatory fees and any call recording, transcription or AI agent minutes come on top. Over a year the number alone costs $25.80 at Twilio, $12.00 at Plivo and from $12.00 at Telnyx; the minutes are most of the bill. If an AI receptionist answers the line, its own per-minute price adds to these; our AI receptionist cost guide covers that side.

Add-ons that change the bill

The rental and the minutes are only the base. The same pricing pages list features you may switch on, and each one is billed separately:

FeatureTwilioPlivo
Call recording$0.0025 a minute, plus $0.0005 a minute per month to store$0.0000 a minute
Answering machine detection$0.0075 a call$0.0000 a minute
Transcription (Twilio)$0.0500 a minuteNot used: row cut at our read
Automatic speech recognition (Plivo)Not listed in the part we read$0.02 per 15 seconds
Branded calling$0.12 a callNot in the part of the page we read
Emergency calling$0.75 a month per numberNot in the part of the page we read

On our reading, transcription can move the total a lot: at Twilio's $0.0500 a minute, transcribing the 2,000 minutes in the example above would add $100 a month, more than double the $46.15 base. Per-call fees such as branded calling weigh more on short calls; at $0.12 a call it costs more than transcription for calls under 2.4 minutes. Plivo prices speech recognition by the 15 seconds rather than by the minute, so compare on the length of your typical call. Twilio also lists a $15 trial credit "to buy a phone number, test Voice features." If you run many numbers, Telnyx's tiers apply once you buy more than 50 a month: $0.79 for the next 200, then $0.50, $0.39, and $0.25 a month from 5,000.

Recording calls also raises consent questions; our call recording laws by state guide lists them. Branded calling has its own cost guide: branded caller ID cost.

800 numbers, vanity numbers and the FCC rules

Telnyx prices numbers in the 800 prefix separately: "800 TFN numbers $500 OTC (covers 12-mo term) + $40 MRC (after 12 months)," with a required 12-month commitment. So an 800 number there costs $500 in year one and $480 a year after that, against from $12 a year for an ordinary toll-free number from the same carrier.

Federal rules shape how these numbers are handed out. Under 47 CFR 52.101, a toll-free number is managed by a "Responsible Organization ("RespOrg")," the entity a subscriber chooses "to manage and administer the appropriate records in the toll free Service Management System." And 47 CFR 52.107 bans hoarding and brokering: "Toll free subscribers shall not hoard toll free numbers," and "No person or entity shall acquire a toll free number for the purpose of selling the toll free number to another entity or to a person for a fee." The ban does not apply "to toll free numbers assigned via competitive bidding."

On our reading, that means an offer to sell you a specific vanity toll-free number for a fee deserves a question about where the number came from; buying through a carrier at its listed price avoids that question. This is general information, not legal advice.

Texting from a toll-free number

At Twilio, a toll-free number can send texts only after verification. Twilio's help center says: "As of January 31, 2024, messages sent from any unverified (Restricted or Pending) Toll-Free phone numbers (TFPN) are blocked. Only fully verified Toll-Free phone numbers are eligible to send messages." Blocked messages return Error 30032 "and are subject to messaging fees."

Our toll-free verification policy URLs guide covers the verification form. The texting rules themselves, including consent, are in our 10DLC registration cost and TCPA opt-out requirements guides.

Which number to pick

Our suggestions, from the prices above:

  • Most callers in one area: a local number, at a lower inbound rate.
  • Callers nationwide, or a number printed on ads: a toll-free number; budget for the inbound minutes, not the $1 to $2.15 rental.
  • Texting: verify the toll-free number before the first campaign; at Twilio, unverified numbers are blocked.
  • An 800 number: only if the prefix itself is worth $500 in year one to you.

If the line will be answered by an AI voice agent, see our AI calling for home services page, our AI answering service for HVAC guide and our AI voice agents compared guide. Prices change; check each carrier's page before you buy.
faqs: How much does a toll-free number cost per month?
At the three carriers we checked on 22 November 2026, a US toll-free number costs $1.00 a month at Plivo, from $1.00 at Telnyx and $2.15 at Twilio, on pay-as-you-go list prices.
Who pays for calls to a toll-free number?

The number's owner pays the inbound minutes, at a higher rate than on a local number. Twilio charges $0.0220 a minute to receive a toll-free call, Plivo $0.0180 and Telnyx from $0.015, while receiving a call on a local number costs from $0.0032 to $0.0085 a minute at the same carriers.
What is the cheapest toll-free number?

Among the three carriers we read, Plivo lists toll-free numbers at $1.00 a month and Telnyx from $1.00, against $2.15 at Twilio. Telnyx's inbound rate starts lowest at $0.015 a minute but varies by the calling number, so compare on your own call volume.
How much does a 1-800 number cost?
Telnyx prices numbers in the 800 prefix at $500 one-time for a 12-month term, then $40 a month. Ordinary toll-free numbers from the same carrier start at $1.00 a month.
Can you buy a vanity toll-free number from someone?

FCC rule 47 CFR 52.107 says no person may acquire a toll-free number to sell it for a fee, and toll-free subscribers may not hoard numbers. The rule does not apply to numbers assigned through competitive bidding.
Can a toll-free number send text messages?

At Twilio, only once it is verified. Twilio says that since 31 January 2024, messages from unverified toll-free numbers are blocked and only fully verified toll-free numbers can send messages. Telnyx charges $0.10 a month to add SMS and MMS to a number.
